newsitem.title: FRANCE: French grain crops seen escaping frost damage.
newsitem.headline: French grain crops seen escaping frost damage.

text.p: French crop experts said on Friday that it was unlikely significant grain crop damage would occur as a result of below-freezing temperatures recorded in France since December 27.
In a statement the ITCF crop quality institute explained that because temperatures went down progressively, most crops had time to adapt.
In addition most crops had already reached a development stage that made them more frost-resistant.
Experts said winter oats and durum wheat were the most vulnerable varieties but were absent from the hardest hit areas.
Patches where farmers made late sowings of winter soft wheat and barley may be at risk.
Experts stressed that if temperatures were to hold below freezing or if temperatures following the frost remained low it would take a while to assess possible crop damage on these patches.
